title: Accord counterparties fall into two structural classes: three-entity Prime stacks and bare Executor Agents
content:
The "Parties To The Accord" subdocuments reveal a consistent split in how counterparties are constituted. Token-issuing Stars are three-entity stacks: Keel "comprises the Keel Prime Agent, Keel Foundation, and Development Company" (A.2.8.2.3.1.1.2); Skybase the same shape (A.2.8.2.7.1.1.2); Osero is "the Osero Prime Agent, Osero Foundation, and Stablewatch" (A.2.8.2.6.1.1.2); Obex is "the Obex Prime Agent, Rubicon, and Treadstone" (A.2.8.2.4.1.1.2). Grove is a two-entity variant: Prime Agent plus Foundation (A.2.8.2.10.1.1.2).

Operational Executor Agents are single entities: Amatsu "comprises the Amatsu Executor Agent" (A.2.8.2.8.1.1.2) and Ozone likewise (A.2.8.2.9.1.1.2).

The correlation is with tokenomics, not with size. Parties that will issue their own token and hold a treasury need a Foundation (a legal person that can hold assets and contract off-chain) and a Development Company (an employer). Parties that only render services to other Agents need neither, because their revenue is USDS from Sky and their output is labour.

Reading the party composition is therefore a fast way to classify a counterparty's intended role before reading its substantive terms — and it predicts which Accord sections will exist at all, since single-entity Accords carry no Tokenomics subdocument.
description: Keel, Skybase and Osero each comprise a Prime Agent plus a Foundation plus a Development Company; Amatsu and Ozone comprise only an Executor Agent
